350487.title: Tree-symmetrization identity for the Joyce potential
350487.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be an unrooted, unlabeled tree with $n$ vertices, and let $K_\mathcal{T}(\{\gamma_i,t_i\})$ be the tree kernel defined by the product over its oriented edges. Write ${\rm Sym}$ for symmetrization over the labels. For each labeling $\ell:v\mapsto i\in[1,n]$ of the vertices, orient every edge from $v$ to $v'$ whenever $\ell(v)<\ell(v')$. **Tree-symmetrization conjecture.** For each unrooted, unlabeled tree $\mathcal{T}$ one has

$$
{\rm Sym}\,K_\mathcal{T}(\{\gamma_i,t_i\})=\frac{1}{(4\pi\mathrm{i})^{n-1}}\,{\rm Sym}\,\Biggl[\left(\sum_{\rm labels}\prod_{e:i\to j}\langle\gamma_i,\gamma_j\rangle\right)\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{t_i t_{i+1}}{t_{i+1}-t_i}\Biggr].
$$

The identity is proposed to establish that the tree expansion of the Fourier modes of the Joyce potential agrees with the expression obtained from the Joyce construction, thereby relating the factorized and tree-based descriptions of the heavenly metric.

350964.title: The odd-width admissible-partition character identity for $C_{(1)}_\ell$
350964.literal_statement:
Let $\ell\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal N_{2\ell+1}$ be the array of $\ell$ copies of $\mathbb N$ together with the odd positive integers, arranged in $2\ell+1$ rows, and let $f_a$ denote the frequency of the part $a$ in a colored partition. For parameters $k_0,\dots,k_\ell$, write $k=k_0+\cdots+k_\ell$, and let $D(k_0+1,k_1+1,\dots,k_\ell+1)$ and $\Delta(k_1+1,\dots,k_\ell+1)$ denote the indexing sets used in the principally specialized character.

**The odd-width character identity.** The principally specialized character

$$
\frac{\prod_{a\in\{0\}^\ell\cup D(k_0+1, k_1+1,\dots, k_\ell+1);\, b\in \Delta( k_1+1,\dots, k_\ell+1);\, j\equiv a,\pm b\mod (2\ell+2k+2)}(1-q^j)}{\prod_{j\, \text{odd}}(1-q^j)\prod_{j\in\mathbb N}(1-q^j)^\ell}
$$

is the generating function for the number of $(k_0,k_1,\dots,k_\ell)$-admissible colored partitions

$$
n=\sum_{a\in\mathcal N_{2\ell+1}}f_a\cdot a.
$$

This identity connects principally specialized $C_\ell^{(1)}$-characters with colored-partition generating functions; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
350964.assessment: All-rank/all-level affine character and admissibility identity is not finite from discrete metadata.

355350.title: Extremal bound for suboptimal $(2d+1)$-union antichains
355350.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $\mathcal{L}(V)$ denote its lattice of subspaces. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{L}(V)$ is a **$(2d+1)$-union antichain** if it is an antichain whose union of any $2d+1$ members is not a member of the family. Assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is not contained in any optimal $(2d+1)$-union antichain and that $2d+1<n$. Let $\left[n\atop d\right]$ denote the Gaussian binomial coefficient and let $\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$ be the family defined in the source. **Extremal bound conjecture.**

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \left[n\atop d\right]-q\left[d\atop 1\right].
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$. This conjecture seeks the sharp size bound and equality characterization for suboptimal $(2d+1)$-union antichains; the notation $\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$ is not defined in the supplied context, and its structure and the conjecture's resolution require verification.

356630.title: Gessel's equidistribution conjecture for permutations with disjoint cycle types
356630.literal_statement:
Let $\mu\vdash m$ and $\nu\vdash n$ be integer partitions with no common part. Let $\pi$ and $\sigma$ be permutations of cycle types $\mu$ and $\nu$, respectively, with disjoint supports. Let $A_{\pi,\sigma}$ be the subset of the conjugacy class of cycle type $\mu\sqcup\nu\vdash m+n$ consisting of the permutations for which the relative order of the letters in the union of all cycles of $\mu$ is as in $\pi$, and the relative order of the letters in the union of all cycles of $\nu$ is as in $\sigma$. **Gessel's conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum\limits_{w\in A_{\pi,\sigma}} {\bf x}^{\Des(w)}=\sum\limits_{\tau\in \pi\shuffle \sigma} {\bf x}^{\Des(\tau)}.
$$

This equidistribution identity connects descent enumerators on a constrained conjugacy class with those on shuffles of the two permutations. The conjecture was proved by Gessel, so it is included as a solved result.
356630.assessment: Exact statement is primary Conjecture6.1, declared proved in Proposition6.3, attributed Gessel2021.
